title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: classify Azure RMS protected Office files on Windows (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing, admin paths and PowerShell call are supported, and targeted searches confirm the narrowly stated documentation gaps. Minor corrections concern the government-cloud source and a device-onboarding checklist step without a controls-table row.

claims.claim: According to the roadmap, Endpoint DLP can now classify Office files stored on Windows devices with Azure RMS protection applied.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP can now classify Office files stored in Windows devices that have Azure RMS protection applied.

claims.claim: The roadmap states that classification is triggered when a file is used in applications.
claims.quote: Classification will be triggered when file is used in applications or when just-in-time classification is enabled

claims.claim: The roadmap also states that classification is triggered when just-in-time classification is enabled.
claims.quote: Classification will be triggered when file is used in applications or when just-in-time classification is enabled

Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this RMS-protected Office-file classification capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP Azure RMS protected Office files classification enable default switch; "Endpoint DLP" "RMS" classification default enabled Office. Opened endpoint-dlp-learn-about, dlp-configure-endpoint-settings and analyze-endpoint-dlp-diagnostic-logs; no description of the new capability.

claims.claim: The Endpoint DLP overview says files are fully scanned for sensitive information types and labels whenever created or modified.
claims.quote: Every time a file is created or modified, it is fully scanned for sensitive information types (SITs) and labels.

claims.claim: The overview says the scanned file is then evaluated against DLP policies and rules.
claims.quote: The file is then evaluated for matches against DLP policies and rules.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The diagnostic-log guide still says DLP cannot evaluate password-protected or encrypted files.
claims.quote: If the RMS status value is `0x1`, the protected file has a password or is encrypted. DLP can't evaluate password-protected or encrypted files.

claims.claim: The roadmap description and the diagnostic-log guide give conflicting accounts for RMS-protected Office files.
claims.quote: Guide: "DLP can't evaluate password-protected or encrypted files." Roadmap: "Endpoint DLP can now classify Office files stored in Windows devices that have Azure RMS protection applied."

claims.claim: Roadmap item 503780 lists the same classification capability for GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: 503780: "Endpoint DLP can now classify Office files stored in Windows devices that have Azure RMS protection applied." "clouds": ["GCC", "GCC High", "DoD"]
claims.fix: Add https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/roadmap?id=503780 to sources for the government-cloud statement; the linked wiki briefing is not its evidence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The service description publishes no separate licence specifically for RMS-protected Office-file classification.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "RMS" "license" pricing classification. Opened Microsoft Purview service description and searched its text for Endpoint DLP, RMS and protected Office; the Endpoint DLP table lists inclusion but no separate classification licence.

claims.claim: The service description publishes no separate meter for this classification capability.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "RMS" "license" pricing classification. Read the Endpoint DLP section of Microsoft Purview service description and searched its text for RMS and protected Office; no meter specific to this capability is named.

claims.claim: Devices for JIT monitoring is at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection > Choose which locations to monitor > Devices.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. Select Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection. Under Choose which locations to monitor, select the checkbox next to Devices.

claims.claim: No automation operation for selecting Devices as a JIT monitoring location is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP just-in-time protection PowerShell Set-PolicyConfig JIT fallback action settings API. Opened endpoint-dlp-get-started-jit and Set-PolicyConfig; searched the reference for JIT and Just; no operation for this setting.

claims.claim: JIT deployment requires antimalware Client version 4.18.23080 or later.
claims.quote: Before you can deploy just-in-time protection, you must first deploy antimalware Client version 4.18.23080 or later.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Administrators should allow at least an hour for changes to JIT settings to reach client devices.
claims.quote: Allow at least an hour for JIT setting updates, including disabling JIT, to be pushed to client devices.

claims.claim: The fallback setting is at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection > Fallback action in case of failure.
claims.quote: Select Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection. Under Fallback action in case of failure, select Allow users to complete actions.

claims.claim: No automation operation for changing the JIT fallback action is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "just-in-time" "PowerShell" "fallback"; Endpoint DLP JIT fallback action settings API. Read JIT deployment guidance and Set-PolicyConfig; no parameter or endpoint documents changing this fallback setting.

claims.claim: The fallback options are Allow users to complete actions and Block users from completing actions.
claims.quote: Selecting Allow users to complete actions or Block users from completing actions doesn't change whether JIT Block is triggered.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The fallback action controls Endpoint DLP enforcement when classification fails under JIT protection.
claims.quote: The Allow users to complete actions or Block users from completing actions setting controls Endpoint DLP enforcement when classification fails.

claims.claim: Choosing the fallback action does not change whether JIT Block is triggered.
claims.quote: Selecting Allow users to complete actions or Block users from completing actions doesn't change whether JIT Block is triggered. Blocking by JIT is applied if the user is in scope.

claims.claim: Windows path exclusions is at Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > File path exclusions for Windows.
claims.quote: To configure path exclusions in DLP settings, go to Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > File path exclusions for Windows.

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig -EndpointDlpGlobalSettings @(@{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="<file path>"}) configures an endpoint path exclusion.
claims.quote: Use the Set-PolicyConfig cmdlet to modify the endpoint restrictions that are configured in the organization. The EndpointDlpGlobalSettings parameter specifies the global endpoints. Example values: `@{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="C:\Windows";}`

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig is a Security & Compliance PowerShell cmdlet.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: controls: scope; controls[2].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The displayed settings are centrally configured tenant controls, and endpoint settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.
claims.quote: Centrally configured settings control many aspects of endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) behavior. These settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.

claims.claim: Files in excluded locations are not audited or subject to DLP policy enforcement.
claims.quote: Files in excluded locations aren't audited. Any files that you create or modify in those locations aren't subject to DLP policy enforcement.

claims.claim: Windows endpoint path exclusions prevent classification and protection, unlike JIT path exclusions which exclude only JIT evaluation.
claims.quote: File path exclusions in JIT only excludes specific file paths from JIT protection. File path exclusions for Windows setting prevents Purview from applying Endpoint DLP classification and protection for files under the specified folders.

claims.where: controls[3].ui and api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate UI switch or automation operation for classifying Azure RMS-protected Office files.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "Azure RMS" "enable" "setting"; Endpoint DLP Azure RMS protected Office files classification enable default switch. Read endpoint settings, Endpoint DLP overview and Set-PolicyConfig, searching for RMS and encrypt; no separate switch or operation.

claims.claim: When advanced classification is enabled, the local device sends content to cloud services for scanning and classification.
claims.quote: When you turn on advanced classification, the local device sends content to the cloud services for scanning and classification.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether advanced classification sends content from RMS-protected files to the cloud classification service is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "RMS" advanced classification cloud content. Opened endpoint settings, overview and diagnostic-log guide; advanced classification names Office/PDF support but does not resolve RMS content handling, while the diagnostic guide still says encrypted files cannot be evaluated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters; rationales
claims.claim: Existing device DLP rules determine protective actions for files that are classified and match those rules.
claims.quote: The file is then evaluated for matches against DLP policies and rules. You can then enforce protective actions on those items via DLP policies.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP rules can block copying sensitive files to USB removable media.
claims.quote: Copy to USB removable device: When this activity is detected, you can block, warn, or audit the copying or moving of protected files from an endpoint device to USB removable media.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP rules can block printing sensitive files.
claims.quote: Print: When this activity is detected, you can block, warn, or audit the printing of protected files from an endpoint device.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP rules can block uploading sensitive files.
claims.quote: You can block, warn, or audit when protected files can be uploaded or prevented from being uploaded to cloud services based on the allow/unallowed domains list in Data loss prevention settings.

claims.claim: JIT protection detects and blocks egress activities on monitored files while policy evaluation completes.
claims.quote: Use endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) just-in-time (JIT) protection to detect and block egress activities on monitored files while policy evaluation completes.

claims.claim: JIT protection supports Windows 10, Windows 11 and macOS.
claims.quote: JIT protection for Endpoint DLP supports these devices: Windows 10; Windows 11; macOS (the three most recent versions)

claims.claim: Disable classification excludes file extensions from Endpoint DLP content scanning rather than targeting RMS-protected files separately.
claims.quote: Use this setting to exclude specific file extensions from Endpoint DLP classification. When you add a file extension to this setting, Endpoint DLP doesn't scan content in files with this extension.

claims.where: Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout; What's changing
claims.claim: Devices must be onboarded to serve as locations in DLP policies.
claims.quote: You need to onboard all the devices you want to use as locations in your DLP policies.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to confirm device onboarding, but the controls table has no corresponding row.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Confirm that the Windows devices where protected Office files are used are onboarded". Table: JIT monitored locations, JIT fallback action, Windows file path exclusions, and a separate classification switch only.
claims.fix: The At rollout device-onboarding check has no controls-table row. Remove that checklist bullet; retain the documented onboarding prerequisite in Scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Data exposure
claims.claim: The roadmap description addresses classification and its triggers, without describing changes to identities or permissions to open protected files.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP can now classify Office files stored in Windows devices that have Azure RMS protection applied. Classification will be triggered when file is used in applications or when just-in-time classification is enabled

claims.claim: Azure RMS is Azure Rights Management.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Message Encryption is a service built on Azure Rights Management (Azure RMS)
